title: Reporting of Events Involving Participant Health and Safety Occurring at the PACE Center
canonicalText:
[[PA.8001 | Reporting of Events Involving Participant Health and Safety Occurring at the PACE Center | Applies to: PACE | Revised 04/01/2024]]
<<page 1>>
I. PURPOSE
This policy outlines the procedures for notifying the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) of
reportable events involving Participants and their health and safety which occur at the CalOptima
Health Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE) Center.
II. POLICY
A. CalOptima Health PACE Center shall comply with the Adult Day Healthcare Center (ADHC)
  reporting requirements of the State of California for incidents and events involving Participants and
  their health and safety that occur at the CalOptima Health PACE Center.
III. PROCEDURE
A. The CalOptima Health PACE Quality Improvement Manager, or their Designee, shall provide to
  DHCS reports involving reportable events that involve Participants at the CalOptima Health PACE
  Center, including, but not limited to:
  1. Death, injury, and unusual incidents which shall be reported within forty-eight (48) hours by
    telephone to DHCS and to the person(s) responsible for the Participant concerning the death of
    any Participant from any cause, any serious injury as determined by the attending physician, and
    any unusual incident which threatens the welfare, safety, or health of any Participant, such as
    physical or psychological abuse of a Participant by employees or other Participants, or
    unexplained absence of any Participant.
    a. The telephone report shall be followed by a written report to DHCS within seven (7)
      calendar days following such an event.
      i. The CalOptima Health PACE Director, with the assistance of the CalOptima Health
        PACE Medical Director or designee, shall write the report and include the name, age,
        sex, and date of admission of the Participant; the date of event, nature of event,
        physician’s findings and treatment, if any; name of attending physician, and disposition
        of the case.
<<page 2>>
  2. Unusual occurrences, such as epidemic outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes or major accidents,
    which threaten the welfare, safety or health of Participants, employees or visitors, shall be
    reported within twenty-four (24) hours by telephone to the local public health officer and
    DHCS.
  3. Fires, or explosions, that occur in, or on, the premises shall be reported immediately to the local
    fire authority.
  4. Statistical summary of services given on forms developed and provided by DHCS.
  5. Other reports as required by DHCS.
B. The CalOptima Health PACE Director or designee shall monitor compliance of the reporting
  requirements outlined in this Policy.
V. REFERENCE(S)
A. CalOptima Health PACE Contract with the Department of Health Care Services for the PACE
  Program
B. CalOptima Health PACE Program Agreement
C. Title 22, California Code of Regulations, (C.C.R.), §78427
<<page 4>>
IX. GLOSSARY
Department of Health Care Services (DHCS): The single State Department responsible for administration of the federal Medicaid (referred to as Medi-Cal in California) Program.
Designee: A person selected or designated to carry out a duty or role. The assigned designee is required to be in management or hold the appropriate qualifications or certifications related to the duty or role.
PACE Center: The location designated by CalOptima Health PACE at which Participants shall receive PCP services.
Participant: An individual enrolled in the CalOptima Health PACE program.
Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE): PACE is a long-term comprehensive health care program that helps older adults to remain as independent as possible. PACE coordinates and provides all needed preventive, primary, acute and long-term care services so seniors can continue living in their community.
